card: Wallet rebroadcasts of unconfirmed transactions currently use standard network broadcast to all peers even when -privatebroadcast=1 is set. This PR updates periodic wallet rebroadcasts to route through private broadcast instead of standard connections when enabled, preventing transactions intended for Tor or I2P broadcast from leaking node IP addresses after 12 to 36 hours. It also expands wallet submission logging to include both txid and wtxid with the broadcast result.
changed_since_previous: The implementation and full diff are now available; the diff modifies MaybeResendWalletTxs to check -privatebroadcast and updates the functional test wallet_resendwallettransactions.py with --privatebroadcast testing.
evidence: PR description: 'If -privatebroadcast=1 and a transaction is submitted locally with the sendrawtransaction RPC and it is related to the wallet, then the rebroadcasts would use the send-to-all method. Change that to use the private broadcast method.'
problem: When -privatebroadcast=1 is configured, the wallet still rebroadcasts unconfirmed transactions every 12 to 36 hours using the public send-to-all broadcast path. This causes transactions intended to be broadcast only over short-lived anonymized connections to eventually leak the node's IP address over regular peer connections.

risk.why: A flaw in wallet rebroadcast logic or transaction broadcast flags could stall transaction propagation for unmined transactions or leak originating IP addresses.

summary: Direct unconfirmed wallet transaction rebroadcasts through the private broadcast mechanism when -privatebroadcast=1 is enabled. Previously, periodic wallet rebroadcasts defaulted to public broadcast across all peer connections regardless of the private broadcast configuration. The change also improves wallet submission log messages by reporting both txid and wtxid alongside the submission result.
